references.text: Joseph says to Pharaoh's servants that interpretations belong to God — the most direct parallel to his words to Pharaoh in Gen 41:16.
Daniel tells King Nebuchadnezzar that no wise man can interpret the dream, but that there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets — paralleling Joseph's acknowledgment of God's sovereignty.
Daniel emphasizes that the secret was not revealed to him because of any wisdom he has beyond others, but so that the king may receive the interpretation — corresponding to Joseph's humility.
Paul acknowledges that our competence does not come from ourselves, but from God — a parallel to Joseph's humble acknowledgment that the answer lies not with himself.

Peter exhorts believers to speak as those speaking God's words and to serve in the strength God gives, so that God may be honored in all things — reflecting Joseph's attitude that it is God who gives answers.
Direct continuation of the same event confirming that only God gives answers and revelation.
Shows the consequence of God's revelation: Joseph receives authority over Egypt as a result of conveying God's answer.
Sharp theological contrast: Pharaoh acknowledges God's power through Joseph (Gen 41:16) but later refuses to know the Lord (Exod 5:2).
Pharaoh directly confirms Joseph's claim that only God gives wisdom and answers.
